title: Impact of Unemployment Benefit Eligibility on Future Earnings

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy
- Method: Sharp Regression Discontinuity Design (RDD)
- Why: Eligibility for unemployment benefits turns on sharply at an age cutoff. Treatment is determined deterministically by whether age is above the cutoff (treated = 1) or below (treated = 0). The outcome is log earnings two years later. RDD isolates the local average causal effect at the cutoff by comparing individuals just above and just below the threshold.
- Key assumptions:
  - Continuity of potential outcomes at the cutoff: In the absence of treatment, the conditional expectation of future earnings varies smoothly with age at the cutoff.
  - No precise manipulation of the running variable: Individuals cannot sort exactly around the age cutoff to self-select treatment.
  - Correct functional approximation locally: A local linear specification (and checks with quadratic) around the cutoff with a reasonable bandwidth approximates the conditional expectation well.

## 2. R Code
```r
# Complete, self-contained R code that:
# - Reads the CSV file from the path provided
# - Runs the appropriate causal analysis (local linear sharp RDD)
# - Prints a clear numerical result (treatment effect at cutoff)
# - Includes basic robustness checks

# Load required packages
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  if (!requireNamespace("sandwich", quietly = TRUE)) install.packages("sandwich")
  if (!requireNamespace("lmtest", quietly = TRUE)) install.packages("lmtest")
})
library(sandwich)
library(lmtest)

# 1) Read data
path <- "experiments/exp_b/data/s87_data.csv"
df <- read.csv(path)

# Basic checks
stopifnot(all(c("running_var","treated","y") %in% names(df)))
x <- df$running_var
treat <- df$treated
y <- df$y

# 2) Infer cutoff programmatically (midpoint that best separates treated=1 from treated=0)
infer_cutoff <- function(x, d) {
  ux <- sort(unique(x))
  # Candidate cutoffs: midpoints between adjacent unique x's
  cands <- (ux[-1] + ux[-length(ux)]) / 2
  if (length(cands) == 0L) return(median(x))
  misclass <- sapply(cands, function(c0) {
    d_hat <- as.integer(x >= c0)
    mean(d_hat != d)
  })
  c_star <- median(cands[misclass == min(misclass)])
  return(c_star)
}
c_hat <- infer_cutoff(x, treat)

# 3) Local linear RDD estimator with triangular kernel and optional quadratic term
ll_rdd <- function(y, x, d, c0, h, poly = 1, min_per_side = 20, max_h_mult = 0.6) {
  rng <- max(x) - min(x)
  # Expand bandwidth if too few obs per side
  h_use <- h
  expand_factor <- 1.2
  while (TRUE) {
    xc <- x - c0
    w <- pmax(0, 1 - abs(xc) / h_use) # triangular kernel
    keep <- which(w > 0)
    if (length(keep) < (2 * min_per_side + 4)) {
      # not enough total obs, expand
      if (h_use >= max_h_mult * rng) break
      h_use <- min(max_h_mult * rng, h_use * expand_factor)
      next
    }
    n_left <- sum(w > 0 & xc < 0)
    n_right <- sum(w > 0 & xc >= 0)
    if ((n_left < min_per_side || n_right < min_per_side) && h_use < max_h_mult * rng) {
      h_use <- min(max_h_mult * rng, h_use * expand_factor)
    } else {
      break
    }
  }
  xc <- x - c0
  w <- pmax(0, 1 - abs(xc) / h_use)
  keep <- which(w > 0)
  dat <- data.frame(y = y[keep], d = d[keep], xc = xc[keep])
  if (poly == 1) {
    fit <- lm(y ~ d + xc + d:xc, data = dat, weights = w[keep])
    vc <- sandwich::vcovHC(fit, type = "HC1")
    ct <- lmtest::coeftest(fit, vcov. = vc)
    est <- unname(ct["d", "Estimate"])
    se <- unname(ct["d", "Std. Error"])
  } else {
    dat$xc2 <- dat$xc^2
    fit <- lm(y ~ d + xc + d:xc + xc2 + d:xc2, data = dat, weights = w[keep])
    vc <- sandwich::vcovHC(fit, type = "HC1")
    ct <- lmtest::coeftest(fit, vcov. = vc)
    est <- unname(ct["d", "Estimate"])
    se <- unname(ct["d", "Std. Error"])
  }
  out <- list(
    est = est,
    se = se,
    ci_lo = est - 1.96 * se,
    ci_hi = est + 1.96 * se,
    pval = 2 * pmin(1, pnorm(abs(est / se), lower.tail = FALSE) * 2), # conservative
    n_left = sum(w > 0 & xc < 0),
    n_right = sum(w > 0 & xc >= 0),
    h = h_use,
    poly = poly
  )
  return(out)
}

# 4) Baseline bandwidth and robustness bandwidths
range_x <- max(x) - min(x)
# Use simple rule: 20% of running variable range
h0 <- 0.20 * range_x
h_small <- 0.15 * range_x
h_large <- 0.25 * range_x

# 5) Run baseline local linear RDD
base <- ll_rdd(y, x, treat, c_hat, h0, poly = 1)

# 6) Robustness checks
# - Bandwidth sensitivity
rb_small <- ll_rdd(y, x, treat, c_hat, h_small, poly = 1)
rb_large <- ll_rdd(y, x, treat, c_hat, h_large, poly = 1)

# - Quadratic polynomial within baseline bandwidth
rb_quad <- ll_rdd(y, x, treat, c_hat, h0, poly = 2)

# - Placebo cutoffs (shift cutoff by +/- 10% of range)
shift <- 0.10 * range_x
c_plus <- c_hat + shift
c_minus <- c_hat - shift
# Truncate to observed support
c_plus <- max(min(c_plus, max(x) - 1e-8), min(x) + 1e-8)
c_minus <- max(min(c_minus, max(x) - 1e-8), min(x) + 1e-8)
rb_placebo_plus <- ll_rdd(y, x, treat, c_plus, h0, poly = 1)
rb_placebo_minus <- ll_rdd(y, x, treat, c_minus, h0, poly = 1)

# 7) Diagnostics: How sharp is the cutoff (classification accuracy)?
d_hat_at_c <- as.integer(x >= c_hat)
class_acc <- mean(d_hat_at_c == treat)

# 8) Print results
cat("===== Sharp RDD: Effect of UI Eligibility on Log Earnings (2 Years Later) =====\n")
cat(sprintf("Inferred cutoff (c): %.4f\n", c_hat))
cat(sprintf("Treatment classification accuracy at inferred cutoff: %.3f\n", class_acc))
cat("\n-- Baseline (Local Linear, Triangular Kernel) --\n")
cat(sprintf("Bandwidth (h): %.4f | N_left: %d | N_right: %d\n", base$h, base$n_left, base$n_right))
cat(sprintf("Effect at cutoff (treated): %.4f\n", base$est))
cat(sprintf("Robust SE: %.4f | 95%% CI: [%.4f, %.4f] | p-value: %.4f\n",
            base$se, base$ci_lo, base$ci_hi, base$pval))

cat("\n-- Robustness: Bandwidth Sensitivity --\n")
cat(sprintf("h small (%.4f): est = %.4f, se = %.4f, 95%% CI = [%.4f, %.4f]\n",
            rb_small$h, rb_small$est, rb_small$se, rb_small$ci_lo, rb_small$ci_hi))
cat(sprintf("h large (%.4f): est = %.4f, se = %.4f, 95%% CI = [%.4f, %.4f]\n",
            rb_large$h, rb_large$est, rb_large$se, rb_large$ci_lo, rb_large$ci_hi))

cat("\n-- Robustness: Quadratic Specification --\n")
cat(sprintf("Poly = 2, h = %.4f: est = %.4f, se = %.4f, 95%% CI = [%.4f, %.4f]\n",
            rb_quad$h, rb_quad$est, rb_quad$se, rb_quad$ci_lo, rb_quad$ci_hi))

cat("\n-- Placebo Cutoffs --\n")
cat(sprintf("Cutoff +10%% range (c = %.4f): est = %.4f, se = %.4f, 95%% CI = [%.4f, %.4f]\n",
            c_plus, rb_placebo_plus$est, rb_placebo_plus$se, rb_placebo_plus$ci_lo, rb_placebo_plus$ci_hi))
cat(sprintf("Cutoff -10%% range (c = %.4f): est = %.4f, se = %.4f, 95%% CI = [%.4f, %.4f]\n",
            c_minus, rb_placebo_minus$est, rb_placebo_minus$se, rb_placebo_minus$ci_lo, rb_placebo_minus$ci_hi))

cat("\nInterpretation: The baseline estimate is the causal jump in log earnings at the eligibility age cutoff.\n")
```

## 3. Expected Findings
- Sign: Slightly negative. UI eligibility often lengthens non-employment spells and can reduce accumulated experience, yielding modestly lower earnings even two years later.
- Magnitude: Around -0.03 to -0.08 in log earnings (3–8%), locally at the cutoff. The effect should be robust in sign across reasonable bandwidths and polynomial orders, while placebo cutoffs should show estimates closer to zero.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: The cutoff age for benefit eligibility provides a natural experiment to assess causal impacts.
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: Eligibility for unemployment benefits at the cutoff age increases log earnings two years later.
